claim: The reworked D30 reader is not fail-safe. It still drops many messages sent before the arrival indication that do place the rider at the pick-up, including messages that name the pick-up point or the venue. As a result the fee is upheld automatically where D30 requires at least human approval, and with sparse GPS the outcome becomes UPHOLD R9 where D30 gives ESCALATE_HUMAN R10. There are three causes. (a) Any message ending in '?' that has no first-person word is discarded before any place check. (b) _PICKUP_INSTRUCTION removes everything up to the next punctuation mark, so in an unpunctuated message it also removes a placement that follows the instruction. (c) Place cues are a closed positive list: an unknown place cue returns None, not UNCLEAR. This contradicts the CW-F06 text, the function's own docstring and the round 1 disposition (FID-1, ADV-1, SRC-1, A1B-C-01 all claim 'a place cue or the pick-up or venue name keeps a message in').
action: fixed (A1b defect: D30 did not meet Jasper's 'at least approval'): before_arrival_reading inverted to fail safe; a message is dropped only when positively known not to place the rider; variants V84 to V87 and 24 before-arrival reading cases, plus a corpus check that no self-placement is dropped

claim: Before the arrival indication, placements that depend on context or whose words are unknown are excluded. A 'yes' or thumbs-up answering the driver's 'Are you at the lobby?' is excluded, and so is a rider call (words not recorded). In the wait, the same items go to the reading test (V66, V80, V61). Under D27 (readings that cannot be settled go to a person) and D30 (messages that say the rider is at the pick-up count), these are unsettled placements. Their exclusion is FairRyde's own choice, yet open_items records it inside Jasper's 'done' D30 instead of as an open FairRyde item, which is how the GPS extension was handled (D33).
action: fixed for replies: an acknowledgment answering a driver question before the wait counts (V87); calls before the wait stay excluded (D30 named messages; recorded in D34 as a known limitation)

claim: After Jasper accepted D27 ('the reading rule and its windows'), A1b changed that rule and window. The wait now starts TS_TOLERANCE_S (30 s) before the arrival indication, and an acknowledgment answering the driver's question now reads as unclear. The D27 record still describes the window as it was when he accepted it. The D30 record and the playbook step still use the arrival indication as the boundary. In CW-F06, 'Before the arrival indication' (where questions do not count) overlaps 'During the wait' (where questions are STRONG) for those 30 s, and the text does not say which sentence wins.
action: fixed: D27 records the three post-acceptance changes; CW-F06, D30 and both playbooks use one boundary ('before the wait', TS_TOLERANCE_S before the arrival indication)

claim: The new self-tests leave two pieces of the reworked D30 logic untested. A mutation removes each one and the suite still passes 89/89: (1) the 'ends in ? with no first person' shortcut, the cause of FID2-1(a); (2) the WEAK floor from rider GPS before arrival (D33) in a sparse case. No variant has a message before arrival that both places the rider and asks a question or gives an instruction, which is the shape that fails open.
action: fixed: V91 (sparse driver GPS plus rider GPS before the wait gives R10) and the before-arrival cases cover the question shortcut

claim: The ADV-9 crash fix added engine behavior that no rule card describes. When the booking or assignment record (or scheduled_time) is missing, CW-F01 is resolved as ON_DEMAND with RECORDS_MISSING. The CW-F01 card says 'otherwise ADVANCE' and has no missing-record clause, so this element has no source and no FairRyde label.
action: fixed (A1b defect): the engine follows CW-F01 ('otherwise ADVANCE') when records are missing, and CW-F01 now states the missing-record case with RECORDS_MISSING (FairRyde, GEN-R01)

claim: When D33 rider GPS alone makes the evidence WEAK in a sparse case, the R10 'plain' text tells both parties 'the rider disputes presence or says they were at the pick-up'. In that case the rider did neither: the statement does not contest and there is no message. CW-R12's parenthetical likewise covers only the rider being 'placed' under D30, not D33 GPS.
action: fixed: R10 plain text and CW-R12 (EN and zh) cover messages and phone GPS from before the wait (D30, D33)

claim: Two order and data-error gaps remain in the round 1 fixes that are marked fixed. (1) ADV-5(b): when the only driver_assigned record is timestamped after the arrival (a data error), the D30 window is empty. A clear placement before arrival is then dropped silently, with no flag. (2) The new acknowledgment context in read06 takes prev[-1] in list order rather than time order, so an unsorted chat log decides the reading.
action: fixed (A1b defect): chat sorted by time for the context check; an assignment stamped after the arrival falls back to the booking and flags RECORDS_MISSING (V88)

claim: The round 1 CRITICAL (SRC-1, ADV-1, FID-1) is still open. The reference engine still drops many messages sent before the arrival indication that place the rider at a location, and then upholds the fee automatically. CW-F06 says a message counts when it 'carries another place cue that cannot be settled'. The D30 record and CW-F06 say 'a fee upheld on the merits always needs approval', and the D27 record says 'never an automatic uphold'. All three claims are false for these messages, and so is the owner's D30 'at least human approval'. before_arrival_reading only keeps a message whose remainder matches the short _PLACE_WORDS list or the venue name, and returns None for everything else. Its fail-safe default is the opposite of rider_contact_reading's. A second path loses placements too: any message ending in '?' with no first-person pronoun is dropped whole, even when it places the rider.
action: fixed (A1b defect: D30 did not meet Jasper's 'at least approval'): before_arrival_reading inverted to fail safe; a message is dropped only when positively known not to place the rider; variants V84 to V87 and 24 before-arrival reading cases, plus a corpus check that no self-placement is dropped

claim: Row R10's plain text is shown to both parties as the reason a person decides. It says the rider 'disputes presence or says they were at the pick-up'. Under D30 and D33, R10 now also fires when the rider neither disputes nor says anything: rider GPS before arrival only (D33), or a message that only may place the rider, with a non-contesting statement. For those cases the wording is false.
action: fixed (same as FID2-6)

claim: Round 1 (SRC-2, FID-3) separated the GPS extension (D33) from Jasper's D30 in the CW-F06 statement and source note. Three other changed texts still attribute pre-arrival placement, which includes rider GPS, to D30 alone, and they leave out the 'may place' messages. The CW-R12 zh also states as a fact what the English states as evidence.
action: fixed (same as FID2-6); DT credibility note names D33

claim: After Jasper accepted the D27 reading rule 'and its windows', the round 1 fixes changed both. The wait window now starts TS_TOLERANCE_S before the arrival indication. An acknowledgment that answers a driver question now counts as a reading, and 'down', 'out' and 'there' are no longer filler. The D27 record still describes the old window, and nothing records these as FairRyde changes made after the owner's acceptance. The CW-F06 credibility_note also still gives the old window start.
action: fixed (same as FID2-3)

claim: The playbook steps that KB appliers follow, and the D30 record, still put the boundary between the pre-arrival window and the wait at the arrival indication itself. Before it, questions and contests do not count. CW-F06 and the engine now start the wait TS_TOLERANCE_S earlier, where a question or contest is STRONG.
action: fixed: playbook notes and D30 name the TS_TOLERANCE_S boundary

claim: The new acknowledgment exception does not say what an acknowledgment that answers the driver's question is. The English 'unless' (and the zh '除非') can be read as making it counter-evidence (STRONG), while the engine reads it as UNCLEAR (reading test, approval). Card and engine also apply it to any driver question, including ones where a 'yes' admits lateness. That goes beyond the round 1 rationale (ADV-3: answers to a yes/no question about the rider's place).
action: fixed: CW-F06 (EN and zh) says such an acknowledgment reads like a bare yes (reading test)

claim: Calls before the arrival indication are excluded without a recorded source or open item. The stated reason is the same fact that D27 treats as a reading that cannot be settled. Round 1 (FID-6) called this 'a gap to decide'. The builder decided it, and the D30 record lists the choice under Jasper's 'done' decision.
action: refuted by the skeptic: calls before arrival were outside what Jasper accepted and decided

claim: D31's list of the cards from which waiting-fee disputes are decided is still incomplete, although round 1 (A1B-C-04) marked this fixed. It leaves out CW-F03B (the wait start, which can move the outcome), CW-F02/CW-F02B (the anchor), MAT-04 (the filing window) and CW-R10/DQ-06. PB-CW-WAITING uses all of them.
action: fixed: D31 points to PB-CW-WAITING and lists its rules

claim: Before arrival, a message ending in '?' with no first-person word is dropped as 'a question about the driver' before any placement check runs. Subject-less placements followed by a question are therefore never counted. This is the most typical Singlish, Chinese and Malay D30 message, and the fee is upheld automatically. The same text sent in the wait reads PLACES and gives R7 HUMAN.
action: fixed (A1b defect: D30 did not meet Jasper's 'at least approval'): before_arrival_reading inverted to fail safe; a message is dropped only when positively known not to place the rider; variants V84 to V87 and 24 before-arrival reading cases, plus a corpus check that no self-placement is dropped; the question shortcut now runs after the placement check

claim: _PICKUP_INSTRUCTION treats the nouns 'stop', 'park' and 'pick up', and the first-person verb 'wait', as imperative instructions. It deletes the placement from the message, so common Singapore pick-up placements (bus stops, car parks, 'I wait at lobby') are dropped before arrival and the fee is upheld automatically.
action: fixed (A1b defect: D30 did not meet Jasper's 'at least approval'): before_arrival_reading inverted to fail safe; a message is dropped only when positively known not to place the rider; variants V84 to V87 and 24 before-arrival reading cases, plus a corpus check that no self-placement is dropped; pick-up instructions are stripped only in imperative position ('I wait at lobby', 'bus stop' kept)

claim: before_arrival_reading is not fail-safe, although its docstring and the round 1 disposition say it is. It counts a message only on a positive list: English place words, the self-place patterns, or the exact full lowercased venue or pick-up name. Anything else falls through to None. Abbreviations, landmarks, partial names, and Chinese, Malay or Tamil placements are dropped and the fee is upheld automatically. The same messages read UNCLEAR in the wait (approval).
action: fixed (A1b defect: D30 did not meet Jasper's 'at least approval'): before_arrival_reading inverted to fail safe; a message is dropped only when positively known not to place the rider; variants V84 to V87 and 24 before-arrival reading cases, plus a corpus check that no self-placement is dropped

claim: Before arrival, neither the engine nor CW-F06 reads a short answer in context. A 'yes', 'ya' or thumbs-up answering the driver's 'Are you at the lobby?' is dropped, and the fee is upheld automatically. In the wait, the rule and the engine read the same answer as UNCLEAR (V66, V80), so approval is required.
action: fixed (same as FID2-2, V87)

claim: The in-wait fix for answers in context (round 1 ADV-3) only checks whether the driver's last message ends with an ASCII '?'. Questions without a mark, with the full-width '？', or followed by a sentence are missed. The rider's 'ok' or thumbs-up then reads NEUTRAL, and the fee is upheld automatically.
action: fixed (A1b defect): the context check looks for a question mark anywhere in the driver's last message, in time order, ASCII or full-width (V89)

claim: RIDER_LATE_CORE counts being 'at the mall/MRT/market/clinic/kopitiam' as lateness. When the pick-up venue is that kind of place (DISP-002's Tiong Bahru Plaza is a mall; VENUES includes an MRT station), a placement reads LATE: automatic uphold in the wait, and dropped before arrival. before_arrival_reading returns None on LATE before it checks the place name.
action: not fixed: pre-existing reader gap from A1, frozen area; recorded as known limitation (1) in D34

claim: If the only assignment record is stamped after the arrival (a data error), the D30 window [d30_from, w_start) is empty. Real placements before arrival are then dropped, and nothing flags the problem: the fee is upheld automatically. Round 1 ADV-5(b) named exactly this case, and its disposition marks it fixed, but only the list-order half was fixed.
action: fixed (same as FID2-7, V88)

claim: Safe direction, but frequent. Routine pre-arrival instructions and plans count as D30 placements, which sends AUTO cases at de711a3 to approval. For several of them the rider is told something false: their message 'says you were already at the pick-up point'. That is what round 1 FID-2, ADV-4 and A1B-C-01 said was fixed.
action: partly: explanations no longer say a planned or future message 'says you were already at the pick-up' (future forms read UNCLEAR); over-counting before the wait remains, safe direction, recorded as known limitation (2) in D34

claim: Safe direction, frequent, and introduced by A1b. The new 'down liao' self-place pattern excludes only 'coming', 'come' and 'going'. Together with dropping down, out and there from _FILLER, this turns very common admissions from LATE (de711a3) into UNCLEAR. They then go to approval in the wait, and before arrival they are counted as D30 evidence 'for your side'.
action: fixed (A1b regression): 'otw down liao' and similar are admissions again (V90)

claim: There is a test coverage gap. reading_check runs READING_CASES and the reviewers' corpus only through rider_contact_reading. before_arrival_reading is exercised by just four messages (V74 to V77), so several of the corpus's own P placements are dropped before arrival without any test failing.
action: fixed: before-arrival reading cases and a corpus property check in selftest.reading_check

claim: The round 1 fix ADV-5 starts the CW-F06 wait window TS_TOLERANCE_S before the arrival indication. That change reached the CW-F06 first sentence and the engine, but not the other texts that define the window. In those texts, contests and questions sent in the 30 s before the arrival indication do not count, while the engine counts them as STRONG. CW-F06 itself has both readings: its first sentence starts the wait 30 s early, and a later sentence says 'Before the arrival indication ... questions about the driver ... do not count, because the wait had not started.'
action: fixed (same as SRC2-5)

claim: The new no-crash path (round 1 ADV-9, V83) treats an unrecorded booking type as ON_DEMAND whenever the booking or assignment record (or scheduled_time) is missing. CW-F01, which A1b did not change, says that anything not inferable as on-demand is ADVANCE. GEN-R01 says a condition that cannot be established is not upheld. The fallback appears in no rule card and has no FairRyde label. It also sets RECORDS_MISSING, whose taxonomy label says 'A decisive finding is UNKNOWN', although the booking type is set to ON_DEMAND, not UNKNOWN. CW-F01 is never tested as decisive, and the explanation does not mention the assumption.
action: fixed (same as FID2-5)

claim: The no-crash path for a missing assignment record (V83) produces a party-facing sentence telling both parties that four app records are missing, when only driver_assigned is. The same explanation cites the driver_arrived record as evidence. The group label is old, but this path was a crash before A1b.
action: fixed: the missing-evidence item names only the app events that are missing (confidence unchanged)

claim: When the trip has no arrival indication, the explanation says so and then tells the rider their message was 'sent before the driver marked arrival'. The CW-F06 trace step likewise speaks of 'the arrival indication' that does not exist. The outcome is unaffected (R3 waive).
action: fixed: with no arrival indication the explanation says 'before the wait started'

claim: The R10 plain text that both parties read was widened to 'the rider disputes presence or says they were at the pick-up', but it is still false when WEAK comes only from rider GPS before the arrival (D33) and the statement does not contest. For a message that only may place the rider, 'says they were at the pick-up' overstates it. The rule that both parties are told decided the outcome is also named 'Strong rider counter-evidence', though the evidence is WEAK.
action: fixed (same as FID2-6); CW-R12 not renamed

claim: A new party-facing generic-assumption item is ungrammatical when only rider GPS is decisive.
action: fixed: 'phone GPS was read'

claim: The D27 record was not brought in line with the round 1 fixes. Its 'changed' text still claims that unsettled readings are 'never an automatic uphold'. Round 1 (FID-5, ADV-6, A1B-C-07) corrected this in CW-F06 and D30 to exclude MAT-04 and policy gaps, but not here. The decide field says Jasper accepted 'the reading rule and its windows', but A1b then changed both (acknowledgments answering the driver's question now read UNCLEAR; down, out and there are no longer filler words; the window starts TS_TOLERANCE_S earlier), and nothing records that these came after his acceptance.
action: fixed (same as FID2-3, with the MAT-04 and policy-gap exception)

claim: The annotation workbook's AUTO window falls back to the wait start when there is no driver_assigned event. CW-F06 and the engine fall back to the booking. A D30 message is then left out of rider_contacts and rider_side_evidence, although the engine counts it.
action: fixed: the annotation workbook falls back to the booking before the wait start

claim: D31's list of the rule cards that waiting fees are read from is still incomplete (round 1 A1B-C-04 raised this and the disposition calls it fixed). It leaves out the wait anchor and the wait-start rule that PB-CW-WAITING uses, including CW-F03B, a D-rated FairRyde rule.
action: fixed (same as SRC2-8)

claim: Some engine labels and comments still describe the old CW-F06 window or reason. The F-RIDER-EVIDENCE finding's params (printed in the trace findings table) omit TS_TOLERANCE_S, which CW-F06 now uses and the sensitivity table lists under CW-F06. The comments at 766 and 775 still say the window runs from the arrival indication to the cancellation. The comment at 795 keeps the reason 'the driver had not arrived yet', which round 1 SRC-5 replaced with 'the wait had not started'. The AUTH-05 completeness check still counts rider contacts from t_arr only, so a counted D30 message is scored as missing rider-side records.
action: fixed: TS_TOLERANCE_S in the finding's params, comments updated, AUTH-05 completeness counts D30 messages
